title: Pre-step failure report emits steps:null and step_index -1
description:
Build 6930d36. Repro: scenario with target.mode=connect pointing at a dead port, `./godot-stagehand run sc/s.json --out-dir out`. out/report.json contains `"steps": null` and `"failure": {"step_index": -1, "phase": "connect", ...}`, and the human/CLI line reads `failed at connect step -1 (connection): ...`. Expected: `"steps": []` and a location string without a bogus index (e.g. `connect phase`), with step_index omitted/null in JSON when there is no step. Also of note in the same report: `target` records only `{"mode": "connect"}` -- the port/host that failed to connect are absent because report.Target.Port is only filled from a live session (internal/scenario/runner.go:132), which makes a connection-failure report harder to triage.

title: rpc-trace teardown calls alias step-0 index
description:
Build 5c22cb0. Ran `godot-stagehand run testdata/scenarios/smoke.json --out-dir DIR` against real Godot 4.6.2 (passed, 10/10). rpc-trace.json step indices come out as `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,0]` — the trailing 0 is the teardown step's set_property RPC, indistinguishable from steps[0]'s RPC.

Cause: internal/scenario/trace.go:14-21 `TraceCall` records only `Seq/Step/Method/...` with no phase field, and `tracer.setStep(index)` (trace.go:51) is called with the per-phase loop index for both the `step` and `teardown` phases (internal/scenario/runner.go:138,:168 pass `phase` to the report but not to the tracer). The report.json and junit.xml both distinguish phases (report has separate `steps`/`teardown` arrays; junit classnames read `stagehand-smoke.teardown.set_property`), so rpc-trace.json is the odd one out.

Expected: a trace consumer can join each RPC to the step that issued it. Actual: any tool joining trace.calls[].step to report.steps[] silently misattributes every teardown RPC to steps[0]. Suggest a `"phase"` field on TraceCall.

_filed by orchestrator from backlog-drained QA pass_

title: Addon errors not surfaced as MCP errors
description:
## Summary
Most MCP tool handlers do not call `checkGodotResult()` on the raw JSON
returned by the Godot addon. When the addon returns a handler-level error
like `{"error": "Node not found"}`, the MCP response is marked as
success (`IsError=false`) and the error JSON is passed through as plain
text. MCP clients cannot distinguish addon errors from successful results.

## Affected handlers
All handlers in tools_query.go, tools_input.go, tools_method.go,
tools_wait.go, tools_property.go, tools_performance.go, tools_record.go,
and tools_lifecycle.go (handleGetGameState). Only tools_visual.go
(screenshot handlers) correctly calls `checkGodotResult()`.

## Repro steps
1. Connect to a running Godot game via `godot_connect`
2. Call `godot_find_nodes` with `selector: "class:NonExistent"`
3. Godot returns `{"nodes":[],"count":0}` -- this is fine (not an error)
4. Call `godot_get_property` with a selector that matches but a
   property that doesn't exist
5. Godot returns `{"error": "Property not found: bogus"}`
6. Expected: MCP result has `IsError=true` with the error message
7. Actual: MCP result has `IsError=false` with the raw JSON text

## Impact
MCP clients (like Claude) see error responses as successful tool calls,
making automated test flows unreliable -- errors are silently swallowed.

close_reason: done

Expected: the parked call fails promptly with a terminal 'connection lost / gave up' error. title: CI runs 2 of 28 real-Godot tests: the godot-tagged suite under internal/ never gates anything
description:
CI runs 2 of the 28 real-Godot test functions in the repo. The other 26 have
never gated a PR or a release.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:209` (job `scenario-smoke`) is the only place the
`godot` build tag is exercised:

    go test -tags=godot -run '^TestScenarioRunner' -count=1 -timeout=10m .

Two narrowings, both apparently unintentional:

- trailing `.` — root package only
- `-run '^TestScenarioRunner'` — two test names

So CI runs exactly `TestScenarioRunnerSmoke` and
`TestScenarioRunnerFailsWithAssertionExitCode`, both in
`scenario_smoke_godot_test.go`.

## What never runs in CI

Ten files, 26 test functions:

    internal/godotconn/godot_integration_test.go
    internal/godotconn/security_godot_test.go
    internal/launch/quit_on_disconnect_godot_test.go
    internal/launch/same_project_contention_godot_test.go
    internal/launch/security_godot_test.go
    internal/launch/token_mismatch_godot_test.go
    internal/mcpserver/godot_fixture_helpers_test.go
    internal/mcpserver/launch_port_race_godot_test.go
    internal/mcpserver/multi_instance_two_ports_godot_test.go
    internal/mcpserver/set_property_godot_test.go

Including the entire MVP tool surface (`TestSmokeAllMvpTools`, `TestSmokeClick`,
`TestSmokeScreenshot`, `TestSmokeFindNodes`, `TestSmokeGetProperty`,
`TestSmokePressKey`, `TestSmokePressAction`, `TestSmokeRecordReplay`), the auth
and bind-policy boundary (`TestStagehandAuthenticationBoundary`,
`TestStagehandBindPolicy`, `TestVerifyInstanceTokenAgainstTwoRealLaunches`,
`TestLaunchEstablishesAuthenticatedSafeConnection`), quit-on-disconnect
(`TestQuitOnDisconnectSelfQuitsAfterGracePeriod`,
`TestQuitOnDisconnectOptOutKeepsRunning`) and multi-instance port handling.

## Why it matters now

0.3.1 shipped and then produced four bugs on first contact with real games
(sprh, 60sz, e9p9, 0bdy, mt3i), each found by hand. The goal is a release gate
that removes that manual pass. This is the cheapest available step toward it:
the tests already exist and already pass locally — they are simply not wired to
anything.

Note `internal/launch/quit_on_disconnect_godot_test.go` already covers the
quit-on-disconnect area that mt3i lives in. mt3i's specific case (grace timer
fires against an instance that never had a client) is the gap *within* that
file, not a missing file.

## Done when

1. `scenario-smoke` runs the full godot-tagged suite (`./...`, no `-run`
   filter), or an explicit job does.
2. Whatever turns red is either fixed or filed — do not widen the selector and
   simultaneously narrow it back with skips.
3. Runtime is measured and recorded in the ticket. If the full suite is too slow
   for a per-PR gate, split: fast subset per-PR, full suite on release +
   nightly. Do not leave it unwired because it is slow.
4. A guard against silent renarrowing — the selector must not be able to drift
   back to a single package without someone noticing.

## Risk

Unknown how many of the 26 currently pass in CI's environment. Some may need
xvfb (screenshot tests), some may be flaky under runner contention
(`same_project_contention`, `launch_port_race`). Expect this to be a real piece
of work rather than a one-line change, and expect it to find things — that is
the point.
close_reason: Merged 6972c97: scenario-smoke now runs go test -tags=godot ./... with no -run narrowing; 10 previously-ungated real-Godot tests now gate CI; full tagged suite verified green locally twice

title: No call deadlines or WS keepalive: frozen Godot wedges entire MCP server
description:
S1+S2+S3 causal chain. conn.go:198 ReadJSON with zero SetReadDeadline/SetPongHandler in internal/ (grep-verified); only tools_wait.go sets context.WithTimeout (63,116,200) so all other tools block a worker forever; mcp-go stdio pool of 5 exhausts and whole server wedges incl godot_status. Fix: default per-call deadline in callGodotInstance + read deadline + ping/pong keepalive. Ref: docs/audits/2026-07-08-implementation-audit.md

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect Stagehand to a WebSocket peer that accepts a request but never sends a response, or freeze a connected Godot process without closing TCP.
2. Invoke five ordinary tools such as `godot_get_tree` or `godot_screenshot`.
3. Observe each call waits indefinitely because there is no default call/read deadline.
4. Observe the MCP worker pool is exhausted and even status/disconnect stop responding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every non-wait call has a documented default deadline with a deliberate override path.
- WebSocket read liveness uses read deadlines plus ping/pong keepalive.
- Timeout and disconnect remove pending requests and do not leak goroutines.
- `godot_status` and `godot_disconnect` remain responsive when a Godot instance is frozen.
- Tests cover a silent peer, half-open socket, expired call, recovery, and worker-pool saturation.
- Long wait tools preserve their explicit timeout semantics.

title: Connection lifecycle is confusing and finicky in multi-session use
description:
## Summary

The architecture of stdio MCP process → shared WebSocket → single Godot game is unclear to users and causes practical friction:

- Multiple MCP processes can connect to the same Godot game with no coordination
- Stale processes linger in the background when sessions end, and new sessions unknowingly share the game
- No visibility into who/what is currently connected
- No clear "clean slate" workflow — users end up with ghost connections they don't know about

## User Feedback

"Feels hard to set up and finicky in practice."

## Possible Improvements

- Document the architecture clearly (one Go process per MCP client, all share one game via WS)
- Add a `godot_status` tool showing connection state and other connected clients
- Auto-disconnect or timeout idle connections
- Consider a session/lock model so only one MCP client "owns" the game at a time
- Detect and warn if another process is already connected to the same game
- Graceful cleanup when the stdio pipe closes (parent session ends)

title: Legacy Parse() silently misclassifies new selectors
description:
## Summary
The `selector.Parse()` function (legacy API) does not recognize text:,
meta:, or unique: prefixes. When given e.g. "text:Submit", it falls
through to the default case and returns a Path selector with value
"text:Submit" instead of erroring or returning a Text selector.

While `Parse()` is not called in production (all production code uses
`ParseChain()`), it remains exported and available for external callers.
Its silent misclassification is a trap: any external consumer or future
internal caller using `Parse("text:Submit")` would get a Path selector
that queries for a node at path "text:Submit" -- which will never match.

## Repro
    s, err := selector.Parse("text:Submit")
    // err is nil -- no error
    // s.Type == Path, s.Value == "text:Submit"
    // Expected: s.Type == Text, s.Value == "Submit"

## Recommendation
Either make Parse() support all selector types (like
parseSingleSelectorAllTypes does), or deprecate/unexport it so
external callers don't hit this silently.

## Files
- `<repo>/internal/selector/parse.go` lines 86-112

title: Scenario screenshot_diff threshold/pixel_sensitivity unvalidated
description:
Build d244780. internal/scenario/actions.go:101 validates screenshot_diff's `name` and rejects unknown params, but never range- or type-checks `threshold` / `pixel_sensitivity`. internal/scenario/runner.go:337-338 reads them with asFloatOr(v, 0) (actions.go:180), which silently falls back to 0 for any non-numeric value and passes any float straight through.

Repro (no Godot needed, load-time validation only):
  cat > s.json <<'J'
  {"name":"t","target":{"mode":"connect","port":26799},
   "steps":[{"action":"screenshot_diff","with":{"name":"a","threshold":100,"pixel_sensitivity":-5}}]}
  J
  ./godot-stagehand run s.json --out-dir out
Expected: load error like the one `bogus_param` already produces ('unknown parameter ...'), e.g. 'threshold must be in [0,1]'.
Actual: scenario loads fine and proceeds to connect (exit 3, connection error only).

Same for a string value: {"threshold": "0.1"} also loads, and asFloatOr silently yields 0.0.

Impact: threshold > 1 makes the visual assertion vacuously pass forever (DiffRatio <= 100 always true, visual.go:211) — a green test that can never fail. A quoted/typo'd threshold silently becomes 0 (max strictness) instead of erroring. The MCP path already enforces this: internal/mcpserver/tools_visual.go:69-79,171-175 uses mcp.Min(0)/mcp.Max(1) + boundedNumber for both params, so the two frontends disagree on the same contract.

title: MCP numeric params bypass schema Min/Max bounds
description:
Build 2595f5a. mcp-go does not enforce the JSON-schema Min/Max declared on tool params, and the handlers do not re-check them, so out-of-range numbers reach the deadline math and the Godot wire. Confirmed with a probe test in internal/mcpserver:

  timeout_ms=-5000 -> GetInt=-5000 -> deadline = -3s (context already expired)
  timeout_ms=1e15 -> deadline = 1076616h (~122 years), despite Max(60000)
  timeout_ms=1e19 -> GetInt saturates to math.MinInt64 -> Duration overflow -> deadline 2s
  max_depth=1e6 -> sent verbatim to Godot, despite Max(50)

Affected: internal/mcpserver/tools_wait.go:54,108,181 (timeout_ms feeding `time.Duration(timeoutMs)*time.Millisecond + waitDeadlineBuffer` at :62,:115,:200), server.go:48 (max_depth), tools_visual.go:181-182 (threshold/pixel_sensitivity declared Min(0)/Max(1), unvalidated).

Expected: an out-of-range value is rejected with a named-parameter error before dialing Godot. Actual: godot_wait_for_node with a negative timeout_ms returns the generic 'Godot call timed out - the game did not answer' without ever waiting, which misdiagnoses a caller bug as a dead game; a threshold>1 makes every visual diff pass silently. Same class as the already-open get_performance --monitors enum gap, but on the MCP surface.

title: Integrate self-hosted go-ci-report-card, replacing goreportcard.com
description:
goreportcard.com is deprecated, and its badge has been removed from README.md
(2026-07-25). Replace it with the self-hosted https://github.com/mrf/go-ci-report-card:
GitHub Actions runs the checks, GitHub Pages serves a static report. No server,
database, external API or secret.

## This is the single producer of Go metrics (decided 2026-07-25)

Nothing else in this repo computes Go coverage, gofmt rates, vet or build
status for publication. The README badges ticket
(godot-stagehand-readme-status-badges-ez2g) is blocked on this one and consumes
what this emits, so two workflows can never publish two Go coverage numbers that
disagree on the front page.

That imposes two obligations on this ticket beyond a stock install:

**1. Emit the Go coverage percentage in a machine-readable form.** The badge job
has to read it without scraping HTML. A small JSON or plain-text file written
alongside `_site/` (or a workflow output) is enough. If the upstream tool has no
such hook, add one there rather than recomputing coverage downstream.

**2. Measure it with a real Godot binary and the `godot` build tag enabled.**
The stock workflow has no Godot, so its coverage check would see only the
Godot-free subset: the transport, scenario runner and launch paths
(scenario_smoke_godot_test.go, gdscript_suite_test.go, the godotconn integration
tests) are reached only by the tagged and GODOT_BIN-guarded tests. A Godot-free
run scores the Go code that matters least and reports it confidently. Provision
Godot in the report-card workflow the way ci.yml scenario-smoke job already
does, and set the coverage target in config.toml against what is actually being
measured.

## Install steps (from that repo README)

1. Copy `.github/workflows/report-card.yml` and the whole `reportcard/`
   directory into this repo.
2. Edit `reportcard/config.toml`: project name, coverage target, check weights,
   `minimum_score`. `source_dir = "."` is correct here, the root `go.mod` is
   already in place.
3. On GitHub, Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> source **GitHub
   Actions**. Remote/account op, Mark to do.
4. Push to main. Report lands at https://mrf.github.io/godot-stagehand/.

PRs run the same analysis and gate but do not deploy Pages. `_site/` is
disposable and gitignored, so there is no gh-pages branch and no bot commit
noise.

## Default checks and weights

| Check | Weight | Measured by |
|---|---:|---|
| Formatting | 15 | share of files accepted by `gofmt` |
| Go vet | 20 | `go vet ./...` succeeds |
| Build | 20 | `go build ./...` succeeds |
| Tests & coverage | 30 | tests pass, coverage scored against target |
| Module integrity | 15 | `go mod verify` succeeds |

Weighted average, default gate 80.

## Scope boundary

**The tool scores Go only.** It has no view of addons/stagehand, which is a
large share of the shipped product and its own quality surface with its own
GdUnit4 suite. Do not let a green Go-only score read as a whole-project verdict:
label the README link as Go code quality, and leave the GDScript side to the
badges ticket, which measures it separately for the same reason.

**No badge is documented upstream.** That repo README describes a Pages site,
not a shields endpoint. The README link points at the report; the Go coverage
badge is minted downstream by ez2g from the number this ticket exposes.

## Done when

- Report card workflow and reportcard/ directory are in the repo, running on
  push and PR.
- The report renders at the Pages URL and README links to it, labelled as Go
  code quality rather than overall project quality.
- The Go coverage percentage is exposed in a machine-readable artifact that the
  badge job can consume.
- Coverage is measured with Godot present, and config.toml documents what the
  check covers and excludes.
- No goreportcard.com reference remains anywhere in the repo.

93c0bef7b02dddc6cd720732c27c20c6119b4af0 (git describe: v1.1.10-156-g93c0bef7,

## Step 1 — install: clean

`setup` made exactly two additive edits to project.godot, preserving the four
existing plugin entries alongside seven pre-existing addons
(SmartSlicer, aimg_io, applinks, dockable_container, gdgifexporter, keychain):

    [autoload]
    +StagehandServer="*res://addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd"

    +enabled=PackedStringArray(... 4 entries ..., "res://addons/stagehand/plugin.cfg")

Pixelorama's own 13 autoloads rather than appended. Autoload declaration order
is initialisation order, so this changes host init order. If a host's first

prepend is deliberate or incidental to how setup writes the section.

Pixelorama does NOT run warnings-as-errors. project.godot sets no
gdscript/warnings/*=2; it only DISABLES two warnings:

    gdscript/warnings/return_value_discarded=false
    gdscript/warnings/narrowing_conversion=false

So this project cannot reproduce the strict-warnings failure that broke
plugin.gd and editor/setup_panel.gd during Asset Library prep (the precedent
this step was checking for). That failure class needs a different host project,
or a CI-side override of the host's warnings config. Recorded in the design doc
as a missing axis rather than lost.

Not re-run by hand. Mark drove it during the spike, hit the issues above, and
all are now fixed and merged. Rather than produce a one-off shell transcript
that decays immediately, this step is superseded by the host-compat CI job
(docs/design/host-project-compat-suite.md), which runs setup -> launch ->
connect -> drive on every nightly against a pinned SHA. A transcript proves it
worked once; the job proves it keeps working.

Per the ticket's instruction. 87s.20 and 87s.21 both came from here. Neither was
worked around in the demo.

- godot_version was WRONG: manifest said 4.6.3; project.godot declares
  config/features=PackedStringArray("4.6"). Both bug repros ran on 4.6.2.
- LICENSE is MIT — verified by reading it, was "unverified/WebSearch snippets".
- NO git submodules. The manifest's report was wrong; checkout needs no
  --recurse-submodules.
- project.godot IS at the repo root — no project_subdir.
- 13 autoloads, so heavy-autoloads is evidenced here. Not reassigned — moving an
  axis changes what the other candidates are needed for.
- large-project is DOUBTFUL: 21 MB, 1362 tracked files. Re-measure by import

- content-scale is real but NOT declarative: 93c0bef7 has no stretch or

title: Docs lead with --stagehand, which host apps with their own CLI parser reject
description:
Found while running the 87s.18 Pixelorama spike. First real third-party host project, first launch, immediate failure.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-07-25, Pixelorama v1.2-rc2, Godot 4.6.2, Linux)

    godot --path ~/Projects/Pixelorama/ --stagehand

Stagehand itself works — the autoload registers and the server comes up:

    Stagehand: Authentication token: <redacted>
    Stagehand: Server listening on port 26700 (127.0.0.1)

But Pixelorama runs its OWN command-line parser over the same argv, does not
recognise the flag, and aborts:

    ==========
    Unknown option: --stagehand
    ==========
    Time Pixelorama took to open: 2845ms
    Stagehand: Server stopped

Control run, same project, env var instead of the flag:

    STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 godot --path ~/Projects/Pixelorama/ --headless

    Stagehand: Authentication token: <redacted>
    Stagehand: Server listening on port 26700 (127.0.0.1)
    Time Pixelorama took to open: 2570ms
    -> no 'Unknown option', 0 SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error, process still alive
       at a 20s timeout (exit 124) instead of quitting

So the addon is fine and Pixelorama parses clean under it. The activation
MECHANISM is what breaks, and only on host projects that inspect argv.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Godot passes unrecognised args through to the app, so any project that parses
its own CLI — editors, tools, anything with a --help — sees our flag and may
reject it. That is a large fraction of the 'real app' projects that make the
best demos, and it is a 100% failure on first launch with no hint that the env
var would work.

Current docs make the flag the default path and never mention the alternative
where it is needed:
- docs/quickstart.md:95 and README.md:223 both lead with 'godot --path ... --stagehand'
- STAGEHAND_ENABLED appears 3x in README.md and ZERO times in quickstart.md
- No doc anywhere warns that a host app's own parser can reject the flag

## Fix direction

1. In quickstart + README, present STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 as the launch method for
   installing into an existing third-party project; keep --stagehand for your
   own game and the editor toggle (which is fine — it only injects the flag
   into editor play sessions).
2. Add a troubleshooting entry keyed on the literal string users will see:
   'Unknown option: --stagehand' -> your project parses its own CLI, use the
   env var. README.md:343's 'Connection refused' entry is the closest existing
   hook.
3. Consider whether the setup command should detect a host CLI parser and print
   the env-var form in its post-install instructions.

Blocks the demo video (87s.7): the recording opens with launching Pixelorama,
and the naive command from our own quickstart fails on camera.
close_reason: Merged 869b7aa: quickstart + README now lead with STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 for third-party host projects, added an 'Unknown option: --stagehand' troubleshooting entry, and setup guidance emits the env-var form.

title: Synthesized input does not reach embedded Window subwindows (modal dialogs)
description:
Found driving the 87s.18 Pixelorama spike. Pixelorama shows a modal splash dialog on first launch, and Stagehand cannot dismiss it by any input path. This blocks the demo video (87s.7) at the very first interaction.

## Target

/root/Control/SplashDialog — class AcceptDialog (a Window subclass), i.e. an EMBEDDED SUBWINDOW, modal, visible on launch.

## Evidence (verified 2026-07-25, Pixelorama v1.2-rc2, Godot 4.6.2 Linux, stagehand 0.2.0)

1. SELECTOR CLICK — refused, with a good message:

   input click --selector .../Buttons/NewBtn
   -> 'Click target did not receive the event: ... is not the topmost Control
       at (157.0, 200.5)' (code=not_supported)

   That point is the node's own-space centre, not a screen point:
     global_position = (12, 187), size = (290, 27)
     12 + 290/2 = 157 ; 187 + 27/2 = 200.5   <- exactly what was clicked

   The button renders at roughly (394, 390) in the 1280x720 frame.

2. NO CONTENT-SCALE COMPENSATION. /root content_scale_factor = 1.5 (size
   1280x720, so content space is ~853x480). grep over addons/stagehand/ for
   content_scale|get_final_transform|screen_transform|get_screen_transform
   returns ZERO hits — the addon never converts between content and window
   space.

3. POSITION CLICK — silent no-op, which is worse:

   input click --position '{"x":394,"y":390}'
   -> success, clicked_at {394,390}
   -> screenshot after is PIXEL-IDENTICAL; dialog still up.

4. KEY INPUT — also silent no-op:

   input key Escape  ->  {"key":"Escape","success":true}
   -> SplashDialog.visible still true.

5. call_method hide() is refused by the unsafe guard. Correct behaviour, noted
   only because it removes the obvious workaround.

## Reading

Two distinct problems, and (b) is the blocker:

  (a) Coordinates for a Control inside a subwindow are computed in that
      subwindow's space and used as if they were main-viewport coordinates,
      with content_scale_factor never applied.
  (b) Even a correct screen coordinate does not reach an embedded subwindow —
      position click and key both report success and do nothing. Embedded
      Window subwindows have their own viewport and input routing; pushing the
      event at the main viewport never gets there.

I did NOT isolate (b)'s exact mechanism in engine terms — the modal dialog also
legitimately blocks main-window clicks, so 'main-window clicks still work' is
untested here and should not be assumed either way.

## Why it matters

Modal dialogs are everywhere in real Godot apps — file pickers, confirmations,
preferences, first-run splashes. An automation tool that cannot dismiss one
cannot drive a real application past its first screen. This is the single
biggest credibility gap surfaced by the spike.

## Note on failure modes

The selector path REFUSED and said why, which is the right behaviour and made
this diagnosable. The position and key paths returned success while doing
nothing. Silent success is the worse bug; compare godot-stagehand-hgy, which
fixed a different silent gap on the position-click path.

## Relation to vrj.19

phase3-vrj.19 ('godot_click mis-targets under content-scale stretch — viewport
vs window coordinate mismatch') is CLOSED, and finding (a) looks like the same
class of defect surviving or recurring on a real host project. Worth reopening
that investigation rather than treating this as wholly new.
close_reason: Merged 9efe9b6: input_simulator now resolves Control targets inside embedded Window subwindows (content-scale aware) and refuses — with a typed not_supported — events a modal would swallow, instead of silently succeeding. Adds testdata/test_project/test/test_input_simulator_subwindow.gd (234 lines) as the headless reproduction.

title: Research godot-mcp-enhanced and position Stagehand against it
description:
Competitive research on https://github.com/wgt19861219/godot-mcp-enhanced.

## Why this one specifically

The Asset Library survey done for 87s.5 (2026-07-25, filter=MCP sort=updated)
found 12 MCP assets and read every listing blurb as an EDITOR/authoring tool.
'Godot MCP Enhanced' was on that list. But that survey read short listing
blurbs, NOT the source — and 87s.5 itself flags this: 'Safe to position
against, but worth a skim before making an absolute the only one claim in
public copy.'

This ticket does that skim for the one competitor whose name most implies
broader scope. It is the ticket that either earns or retires the
runtime-vs-editor claim we are about to put in front of real users.

## What to answer

1. Does it drive the RUNNING GAME or only the editor? This is the whole
   positioning claim. If it does any runtime automation, our copy changes.
2. Transport and protocol — how does it talk to Godot? (GDScript addon,
   editor plugin, EditorInterface, debugger protocol, something else)
3. Tool surface: what tools does it expose, and how do they overlap with
   ours (find_nodes, click, screenshot, get_tree, evaluate, wait_for_*)?
4. Does it do input simulation, screenshots, or visual diffing? Those are
   our differentiators — confirm they are actually differentiators.
5. Is there a CLI / CI story, or is it MCP-only? Our scenario runner + JUnit
   + exit codes is the CI angle.
6. Activity, license, Godot version support, install path.

## Done when

- A short comparison written into docs/ (a section in growth-plan.md is fine;
  a whole doc is probably overkill).
- An explicit verdict on whether 'drives your running game, not the Godot
  editor' survives contact with the source. If it does not, file the copy
  changes as their own ticket — README.md:9 blockquote, plugin.cfg
  description, and the blurbs 87s.6 will submit to MCP directories all carry
  that claim.

## Note

Read the repo source, not just its README — the whole point is that blurbs
were already surveyed and were not enough.

blog entry below — one asset, five placements.

https://github.com/Orama-Interactive/Pixelorama — open-source pixel art editor,

title: Host-project compatibility suite: drive real third-party Godot projects at pinned revisions
description:
Stagehand is a tool, so its correctness is defined at the boundary with code we do not control. Today the only integration surface is testdata/test_project/ — a fixture we wrote, which therefore shares our assumptions. It has no CLI parser of its own, no modal dialogs and no content scaling, so it cannot catch the class of bug that actually bites users.

Evidence this gap is real, all from a single afternoon against ONE real project (Pixelorama, 87s.18):
- 87s.20 — host app parses its own argv and rejects --stagehand
- 87s.21 — synthesized input never reaches embedded Window subwindows
- /root content_scale_factor = 1.5 with zero content-scale handling in the addon

Zero of those were visible to the existing suite. The whole Go suite was green throughout.

## Scope

1. HARNESS. Reuse internal/scenario — the runner, JSON/JUnit/trace reporters and the existing scenario-smoke CI job already do most of this. This should be new fixtures plus a job, NOT a new framework. Resist building a parallel test system.

2. PINNING (required, not optional — owner's call 2026-07-25). Every host project is pinned to an exact tag or commit SHA, recorded in a checked-in manifest. Never track a third-party main branch: their refactor becomes our red build, and a suite that is red for reasons outside our control is one people learn to ignore. Bumping a pin is a deliberate, reviewed change — and a bump that breaks us is the signal the suite exists to produce. The manifest should record, per project: repo URL, pinned ref, Godot version, and which stress axes it covers.

3. ASSERTION SURFACE — deliberately narrow. Assert only that Stagehand can install, launch, connect, enumerate the tree, drive input, and screenshot. NEVER assert that the host app behaves correctly; their bugs are not ours. A broad assertion surface is the main way this kind of suite rots.

4. PROJECT SELECTION — choose for stress axes, not popularity. Wanted: its own CLI argument parser; modal dialogs / embedded subwindows; a content_scale_factor != 1; custom _input handling; heavy autoload use; a spread of Godot 4.x minor versions. Verify each candidate is GDScript (not Mono/C#) and confirm its actual engine version from its repo rather than trusting reputation. Pixelorama is candidate #1 and already earned its place.

5. CI. Input and screenshots need a display, so this needs xvfb or equivalent — headless alone will not exercise the paths that broke. Decide cadence: every PR is ideal but may be too slow with N cloned projects; nightly plus on-demand is an acceptable fallback. Cache the pinned checkouts.

## Value

This is also the strongest available answer to the 1.0 readiness question: it converts 'nobody outside this repo has ever run it' into a standing, checkable claim, re-verified on every run.

## Note

May want splitting into an epic with per-project children once part 1 is scoped. Filed as one task deliberately to avoid ticket sprawl before the shape is known.

NO CI workflow and no third-party clone — implementation is held behind rules/design-doc-review-gate.md pending Mark's review of the design doc, and cloning host repos is a remote op reserved to Mark. Follow-on epic children are proposed inside the doc.

title: CI grep ERROR pattern causes false positives
description: The GDScript parse check in .github/workflows/ci.yml (line 70) and scripts/test-godot-compat.sh (line 61) use grep -qE 'ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error' to detect failures. The bare 'ERROR' pattern matches any Godot log line containing the word ERROR anywhere, including harmless engine messages during headless startup (e.g. Vulkan/display driver warnings, 'ERROR: Condition ... is true' from the engine internals). This will cause false positive CI failures on runners where headless Godot emits these common startup warnings. The pattern should be narrowed to match only GDScript-specific errors, e.g. 'SCRIPT ERROR' and 'Parse Error', or filter out known benign patterns. Introduced in commits acfaac6 and fb78bc6. title: set_property silently no-ops on falsy values (false/0) while reporting success:true
description:
Downstream report from downstream-project (ks-stagehand-set-property-falsy-noop-1hs, live-confirmed 2026-07-11 during a stagehand capture session).

SYMPTOM: the set_property MCP tool can return {success:true, previous_value:<correct>} while never applying the new value.
- set_property /root/SimManager running=false -> success:true, previous_value:true — immediate godot_evaluate read-back: running still true. Reproduced 3x; sim kept ticking. Masqueraded as a scene-reload state reset for ~30 min of live debugging.
- set_property .../StagehandCamera current=true DID apply (truthy).
- set_property /root/SimManager elapsed_ticks=0 -> previous_value:0, inconclusive (already 0).

HYPOTHESIS (not yet confirmed in code): JSON falsy values (false, 0, empty string, null) dropped in the set_property path — an if value: style truthiness guard or Variant conversion treating false as absent — truthy sets apply, falsy sets silently no-op while reporting success.

SEVERITY: a tool that lies about success corrupts any automated flow that pauses sims, disables flags, or zeroes counters. Downstream downstream-project re-vendors addons/stagehand after this lands (tracked downstream-project-side).

comments.author: mrf
comments.text:
Investigated with direct headless-Godot instrumentation (real WebSocket JSON-RPC round trips against testdata/test_project, Godot 4.6.2), not just code reading.

FINDING (confirmed via instrumentation): the literal repro — a plain script/built-in property silently failing to apply a falsy JSON value (false/0/""/null) — does NOT reproduce against current main. Added a custom Node with typed properties (bool/int/String/Variant) and confirmed all four falsy values propagate correctly end-to-end (Go MCP handler -> WebSocket -> GDScript addon -> Object.set()) and read back correctly. So the "JSON falsy value dropped by a truthiness guard" hypothesis is not what's happening in this codebase today.

REAL DEFECT (confirmed): property_handler.gd's set_property computed `success` from whether the property was *found*, not whether the write actually *applied*. Added a property with a custom setter that silently rejects a specific value (modeling the exact SimManager.running scenario — a guarded setter) and confirmed the pre-fix code reports `success:true, previous_value:true` while the property never changes — the literal "lies about success" bug, just via a different mechanism (guarded setter / read-only property / type mismatch) rather than a falsy-truthiness guard in stagehand's own code.

FIX: set_property now does a post-set read-back and derives `success` from `applied_value == requested_value`. Same {success, previous_value} contract, no new fields.

TESTS ADDED (internal/godotconn/godot_integration_test.go, both registered under TestSmokeAllMvpTools):
- TestSmokeSetPropertyFalsyValues: round-trips false/0/""/null against real properties, reads each back. Passes before and after this fix (guards against a future truthiness regression in the JSON/GDScript pipeline).
- TestSmokeSetPropertyReportsFailureOnRejectedSet: uses a guarded-setter test property. Verified RED against pre-fix code (success:true despite no change) and GREEN against the fix.

Full suite: go vet ./... clean, go build ./... clean, go test ./... all green (godotconn 6.9s incl. new headless tests). Committed locally (not pushed): c84ef41.

title: godot_launch cannot start the Windows GUI binary from WSL (UNC path mkdir fails; WSL path binds loopback)
description:
`godot_launch` cannot start the **Windows GUI** Godot binary from WSL on 0.3.1. Both documented `project_path` forms fail, so the WSL visual-capture path (screenshots, baselines, diffs) has no working `godot_launch`. Headless Linux `godot_launch` is unaffected and works.

Observed live 2026-07-25 against `~/Projects/downstream-game`, server `e96db7c` (0.3.1), addon 0.3.1, `godot_bin=/mnt/c/bin/Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64.exe`, WSL2 NAT (non-mirrored) networking, gateway `172.25.224.1`.

## Failure A — UNC `project_path`

    project_path: "//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu-24.04/home/user/Projects/downstream-game"
    -> Failed to launch Godot: failed to create the import stamp directory:
       mkdir /wsl.localhost: permission denied

The launcher treats `project_path` as a local filesystem path when creating the import stamp directory, so a UNC path resolves to `/wsl.localhost` at the WSL filesystem root. The UNC form is required by the Windows binary — it cannot read `/home/user/...`.

## Failure B — WSL `project_path`

    project_path: "/home/user/Projects/downstream-game", host: "172.25.224.1"
    -> Failed to launch Godot: Godot failed to become ready: timed out waiting for
       Godot WebSocket on 172.25.224.1:43769: context deadline exceeded
       (last dial error: dial tcp 172.25.224.1:43769: i/o timeout)

The process did start (confirmed via `tasklist.exe`: `Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64 PID 27096`). It timed out because the addon bound loopback on the Windows side: `godot_launch` does not set `STAGEHAND_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0` / `STAGEHAND_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` even though the caller passed a non-loopback `host`. `_get_bind_address()` (`stagehand_server.gd:854`) defaults to `127.0.0.1` without them.

## Working manual workaround

Env vars must be declared in `WSLENV` to cross the WSL -> Win32 boundary; 0.3.1's auth token is read from the game's stdout.

    export STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 STAGEHAND_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1 STAGEHAND_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 \
           STAGEHAND_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 STAGEHAND_QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT=0 STAGEHAND_PORT=26700
    export WSLENV=STAGEHAND_ENABLED/w:STAGEHAND_ALLOW_UNSAFE/w:STAGEHAND_BIND_ADDRESS/w:STAGEHAND_ALLOW_REMOTE/w:STAGEHAND_QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT/w:STAGEHAND_PORT/w
    nohup /mnt/c/bin/Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64.exe \
      --path '\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-24.04\home\user\Projects\downstream-game' --stagehand > gui.log 2>&1 &

Then `godot_connect(host=<gateway IP>, port=26700, auth_token=<token from gui.log>)`. Verified end to end: connect, `godot_screenshot` (real frame), `godot_set_property` fov=28.5 with a visibly zoomed follow-up screenshot.

## Suggested fix direction (not yet verified)

1. Do not derive the import-stamp directory from a UNC `project_path` — detect the UNC/Windows form and place the stamp dir somewhere local, or translate via `wslpath`.
2. When `host` is non-loopback, set `STAGEHAND_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0` + `STAGEHAND_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` on the child, and propagate every `STAGEHAND_*` var through `WSLENV` when the target binary is a Windows `.exe`.

Filed from a downstream-game verification pass of the 0.3.1 `set_property` fix (`e7er`) — that fix itself verified good.
close_reason: Merged 684bbc1: UNC import-stamp path translation + non-loopback bind-address and WSLENV propagation for Windows .exe launches

  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"godot_connect","arguments":{"port":1.5,"auth_token":"x"}}}

title: input_mouse clicks never reach Controls under --headless (degenerate ~64x64 root viewport)
description:
Confirmed with a real Godot 4.6.2 binary. Under --headless, get_tree().root.size and DisplayServer.window_get_size() report a degenerate ~64x64 size regardless of project resolution or explicit [display] size overrides. addons/stagehand/core/input_simulator.gd _node_window_position() maps a Control canvas-space position through get_stretch_transform() into window space and feeds Input.parse_input_event(); with content_scale disabled the stretch transform is identity, so window-space coords land outside the real 64x64 viewport. Godot GUI input dispatch silently drops mouse events outside Viewport bounds -> the pressed signal never fires, yet input_mouse returns success:true (it only validates selector+coord math, not delivery). Root cause verified: (1) get_signal_connection_list shows the pressed handler wired; (2) manual emit_signal(pressed) via evaluate RPC increments a counter; (3) the same input_mouse RPC does NOT increment it even after 1s; (4) root.size stays 64x64 with/without [display] override. Any --headless click test has always been unable to verify a real click landed. Suggested fix: route synthesized mouse events through the target Viewport push_input(event, true) with canvas-space coords instead of global Input.parse_input_event()+window-space transform. Surfaced by vv2.13 smoke-test strengthening; TestSmokeClick uses a narrowly-scoped evidence-gated skip so CI stays green until fixed.

title: Unreachable host exits 6 timeout, not 3 connection
description:
Regression from 521c832 (lazy dial). Build SHA b54c719. When the dial itself times out (blackholed/unroutable host rather than a refused connection), every RPC-issuing one-shot command now reports ExitTimeout (6) instead of the documented ExitConnection (3), with a misleading message claiming Godot failed to answer a method it was never reached for. Cause: the dial moved inside lazyCaller.Call (internal/cli/session.go:64-82), so the failure surfaces to gwpop.Execute (internal/gwpop/gwpop.go:281-290), which maps context.DeadlineExceeded to KindTimeout -> ExitTimeout; previously connectionFlags.open dialed up front and produced a *connectionError -> ExitConnection. Repro (verified by building 521c832^ and main tip and running both): STAGEHAND_AUTH_TOKEN=tok ./godot-stagehand find --host=192.0.2.1 --port=26700 --timeout=6s class:Button . Pre-fix: exit 3, 'connect to Godot at 192.0.2.1:26700: ... i/o timeout'. Post-fix: exit 6, 'find: timed out waiting for Godot to answer "query_nodes"'. `connect` is unaffected (it calls ensureConnected directly, still exit 3), so the contract is now inconsistent across commands. The added test only covers the connection-refused path (fast error -> KindTransport -> exit 3), which is why this slipped through. internal/cli/exit.go:11-34 calls these codes a stable contract that CI pipelines branch on.

title: handleConnect closes conn outside mutex
description: In tools_lifecycle.go line 28-30, handleConnect calls s.getConn() (which acquires/releases RLock), then calls existing.Close() without holding any lock, then later calls s.setConn(). Between getConn() returning and Close() completing, another goroutine could also call getConn() and get the same Connection pointer, then attempt to use it (e.g. via callGodot). This is a race condition window. Compare with clearConn() in server.go which correctly holds the write lock while closing. Also compare with handleLaunch which uses the pattern killExistingLaunch() (properly locked) + separate getConn/Close. The handleConnect pattern should use clearConn() instead of the manual get-then-close. Build SHA: 877e8ed. File: internal/mcpserver/tools_lifecycle.go:28-30.

title: Pre-connect validation misses port and limit ranges
description:
Build 5c22cb0. Commit 521c832 ("fix(cli): validate params before dialing Godot, not after") moved param validation ahead of the dial, but two obviously-invalid inputs still slip through to a dial attempt and get reported as connection failures (exit 3) rather than usage errors (exit 2):

  $ godot-stagehand find --port 99999 Node
  error: find: connect to Godot at 127.0.0.1:99999: dial 127.0.0.1:99999: dial tcp: address 99999: invalid port   (exit 3)

  $ godot-stagehand find --port 26799 Node --limit -5
  -> dials, no complaint about the negative --limit (exit 3, connection refused)

Expected: 99999 is out of the 1-65535 TCP range and -5 is not a valid result limit; both should be caught pre-connect and exit 2 with a usage error, consistent with `--port 0` which already correctly exits 2. Actual: the user is told the connection failed, which points at the game rather than at their own flag. Compare internal/cli/session.go:92 which only checks port != 0. Low severity, but it undercuts the exit-code contract advertised in `--help` (2 usage / 3 connection).

title: godot_wait_for_signal — signal-based waiting with timeout
description:
## Feature

Implement `godot_wait_for_signal` MCP tool — wait for a specific Godot signal to be emitted on a node, with timeout.

## Design (from DESIGN.md)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| selector | string | yes | | Node that emits the signal |
| signal_name | string | yes | | Signal to wait for |
| timeout_ms | int | no | 5000 | |

Returns: `{ received, elapsed_ms, args }`

## Implementation

### GDScript (waiter.gd)
- Use one-shot signal connection: `node.signal_name.connect(callback, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT)`
- Start a Timer for timeout
- Return signal args if received, or `{received: false, reason: "timeout"}` if timer fires first
- Clean up: disconnect signal if timeout fires, stop timer if signal fires

### GWP Method
- Method name: `wait_signal`
- Params: `{selector, signal_name, timeout_ms}`
- Response: `{received, elapsed_ms, args}`

### Go MCP Tool
- Tool name: `godot_wait_for_signal`
- Pass through to GWP `wait_signal` method
- Validate selector with ParseChain() before sending

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GDScript handler with one-shot signal + timer timeout
- [ ] Go MCP tool registered with correct parameter schema
- [ ] E2E test with stub (signal received + timeout cases)
- [ ] Integration test: emit a signal from test scene, verify it's captured
- [ ] Edge case: signal emitted before wait starts (should timeout, not crash)
- [ ] Edge case: node freed while waiting (should return error, not crash)

## TDD Protocol

1. Write Go E2E test expecting `wait_signal` GWP method — fails (not in stub)
2. Add stub case, test passes
3. Write GdUnit4 test for waiter signal handler — fails
4. Implement GDScript handler, test passes
5. Integration test with real Godot

description:
## Problem

Setting up Stagehand requires multiple manual steps: copy addon, enable plugin, register autoload, configure MCP client, (Windows) figure out networking. Each step is a place where an alpha tester bounces.

## Solution

Add a `godot-stagehand setup <project_path>` subcommand that does everything `copy-addon.sh` does plus generates the MCP client config snippet.

### Behavior
```
$ godot-stagehand setup /home/user/my-game

✓ Copied addon to /home/user/my-game/addons/stagehand/
✓ Enabled plugin in project.godot
✓ Registered StagehandServer autoload

Add this to your MCP client config (e.g. .claude/settings.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "godot-stagehand": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/godot-stagehand"
    }
  }
}

Run your game with: godot --path /home/user/my-game --stagehand
```

- Replaces `copy-addon.sh` with a Go-native implementation (no bash dependency)
- Detects own binary path for the MCP config snippet
- Detects Windows/WSL and adjusts guidance (host IP, path format)
- Idempotent — safe to run multiple times

- [ ] `godot-stagehand setup /path` copies addon, enables plugin, registers autoload

title: Visual reliability: screenshots, launch/connect, and diffable baselines
description:
## Problem

Downstream projects are starting to depend on Stagehand for visual and interaction verification. Downstream Game exposed the current failure mode: the tool can connect, but screenshots may be empty/grey/non-rendered in WSL/headless/display-mismatch setups, causing agents to loop on game bugs that are really Stagehand/runtime capture problems.

This belongs upstream in godot-stagehand, not vendored per game. Game repos should assert game-specific facts such as Tesla is left; Stagehand should guarantee that screenshot capture, launch/connect, and baseline/diff primitives are reliable and diagnosable.

## Goal

Make Stagehand a trustworthy visual-smoke tool:
- A screenshot of a rendered fixture is non-empty and pixel-meaningful.
- Failures report the real cause: headless/no GPU/no frame/connection path/buffer issue.
- WSL/Linux/Windows launch and connect defaults are documented and tested.
- Baseline/diff APIs are stable enough for downstream game repos to build visual regression harnesses.

## Non-goals

Do not add Downstream Game-specific assertions here. Stagehand should not know about orchards, fog, iPad maps, or Tesla/Oakdale orientation.

## Done

Children below provide a minimal rendered fixture, non-empty screenshot test, launch/connect hardening, visual baseline/diff workflow, and downstream integration docs.

## Task

Add a tiny deterministic Godot fixture scene/project that renders unmistakable colored geometry or UI regions, then add an automated screenshot smoke test that launches/connects, calls godot_screenshot, decodes the PNG, and asserts:
- width and height are non-zero and match the requested viewport or fixture expectation;
- encoded data is non-empty;
- sampled pixels include the expected non-background colors;
- all-black/all-transparent/all-single-color screenshots fail with actionable diagnostics.

## Acceptance

- Test fails before a real rendered frame is available and passes only when pixels are meaningful.
- Works on the supported local display path selected by the implementation.
- Failure message distinguishes no frame/headless/no GPU/transport/buffer problems where possible.
- The test is documented as the canonical upstream proof for downstream game visual smoke work.

title: Addon: self-quit on WebSocket bind failure to prevent zombie instances
description:
## Problem

When a Godot game launches with stagehand enabled (`STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1` / `--stagehand`) on a port already held by another instance, the addon's `_tcp_server.listen(_port)` fails (`stagehand_server.gd:41-45`). It currently `push_error` + `set_process(false)` and **the game keeps running forever with no server** — a headless zombie burning ~500 MB.

Observed 2026-06-01: five stale Windows Godot GUI instances accumulated this way (~2.5 GB), all having lost the race for port 26700; only the first held the server.

Compounding bug (Go side, `internal/launch/launch.go:127-181`): `dialGodotWhenReady` connects to host:port answered by the *first* instance, pings OK, and `Launch` returns success reporting the **newly-spawned PID but a connection to the old process** — no verification it reached the process it spawned. Result: a fresh `godot_launch` silently attaches to a pre-existing squatter (gray screen, empty scene). PID comparison can't fix this across the WSL→Windows boundary (`cmd.Process.Pid` is the WSL interop pid, not the Windows pid).

## Decision (context)

We are NOT pursuing multi-instance/port-isolation (see vrj.9) — visual screenshot testing is single-focused-window by nature, so the single shared game on 26700 is the intended model. Concurrency is managed upstream in the orchestrator via an ownership gate (worktree detection + lease lock in the stagehand skill). This issue is just the hygiene fix so collisions self-clean instead of accumulating ghosts.

## Fix

1. **Addon self-quit on bind failure** (primary): on `listen()` error, `get_tree().quit()` instead of running serverless. GUARD: only quit when launched as a game with stagehand explicitly enabled (`STAGEHAND_ENABLED`/`--stagehand`); the **editor toolbar-toggle** path must NOT quit the editor. Verify the activation source before quitting.
2. (Optional, lower value) Surface the bind failure to the launcher so `godot_launch` errors clearly instead of attaching to a stranger. Likely deferred — the orchestrator gate prevents the collision upstream.

## TDD / acceptance

- Failing test first. `go test ./...` green; `go vet ./...` clean.
- `.gd` changes strict-mode compliant (warnings-as-errors).
- Verify addon does NOT quit the editor when toggled via the editor toolbar.
- Verify a second game launched on an occupied port exits on its own rather than lingering.
close_reason: Merged worktree-addon-bind-fail-selfquit into main (no-ff). Addon self-quits (exit 70) on WebSocket bind failure only for game/CLI launches; editor toolbar-toggle path preserved. go vet/build/test green; GdUnit4 bind test added.

title: godot_launch silently attaches to a pre-existing instance on the port (no spawned==connected verification)
description:
## Summary
`godot_launch` can report success while actually connected to a DIFFERENT, pre-existing Godot instance that already holds the port — returning the newly-spawned PID but a connection to the old process. There is no verification that the process we spawned is the one we connected to.

## Evidence (downstream-game, 2026-06-01)
- Five stale Godot GUI instances were running; PID 14268 held port 26700. A fresh `godot_launch` returned `pid:115454` (the newly spawned process) but the connection was to 14268 (confirmed: `physics_ticks` ~11 min of runtime on a "just launched" game; netstat showed 14268 ESTABLISHED with the WSL client). The new process failed to bind the port (addon `listen()` error path) and sat as a serverless zombie.
- Net effect: the user believes they are testing a fresh launch but are driving a stale/old instance (gray screen, empty scene in our case).

## Root cause (internal/launch/launch.go ~127-181)
`dialGodotWhenReady` connects to host:port and pings; whoever owns the port answers OK, so `Launch` returns success with `cmd.Process.Pid` but a connection to the squatter. PID comparison cannot fix this across the WSL->Windows boundary (`cmd.Process.Pid` is the WSL-interop pid, not the Windows pid).

## Proposed fix
Have the launcher prove it reached the process it spawned: generate a random nonce per launch, pass it via env (e.g. `STAGEHAND_INSTANCE_TOKEN`), have the addon echo it in the `ping` response, and assert it matches before returning success. On mismatch, fail clearly ("connected to a different Stagehand instance; the process we launched failed to bind port N — free the port or pick another"). Optionally pre-dial the port and error early if it is already occupied.

## Related
- Addon self-quit on bind failure: godot-stagehand-phase3-vrj.17.6 (prevents the zombie side).
- Decision: we are NOT pursuing multi-instance/port isolation (vrj.9) — single shared game is intended; concurrency is gated upstream in the orchestrator. This issue is purely about not silently attaching to the wrong process.

## Impact
MEDIUM — silent wrong-instance attach caused a long misdiagnosis this session.

title: godot_click mis-targets under content-scale stretch (viewport vs window coordinate mismatch)
description:
## Summary
`godot_click` with a selector misses its target when the project uses content-scale stretch (window size != render/viewport size). Node rects are reported in viewport/content-scale space, but the click warp is applied in window space, so selector clicks land off-target by the stretch ratio.

## Evidence (downstream-game, 2026-06-01)
- Window size: 1280x720. content_scale_size / viewport: 1920x1080 (stretch factor 1.5x). Confirmed via `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` = (1920,1080), `get_window().size` = (1280,720).
- The "SAVED RUN FOUND" dialog CONTINUE Button: `global_position`=(792,609), `size`=(160,40) -> viewport-space center (872,629).
- `godot_click(selector:"text:CONTINUE")` reported `success:true, clicked_at:(960,544.5)` but the dialog did NOT dismiss.
- Manual `godot_click(position:{872,629})` (the button center in viewport space) -> also no-op.
- Manual `godot_click(position:{581,419})` (= 872*1280/1920, 629*1280/1920, i.e. the button center scaled into WINDOW space) -> SUCCESS, save loaded.

## Diagnosis
- `godot_find_nodes` / node `global_rect` are in viewport/content-scale coordinates (1920x1080).
- `godot_click` interprets `position` (and computes selector-target centers) and warps the mouse in WINDOW coordinates (1280x720).
- When `window_size != content_scale_size`, selector-based clicks (and any caller passing rect-derived coords) miss by the stretch ratio. Many real games render at a fixed internal resolution and stretch — this breaks click targeting for all of them.

## Proposed fix
Translate node-rect coordinates into the input/window space before warping (multiply by `window.size / viewport.get_visible_rect().size`), OR deliver the synthetic input event in the viewport's input coordinate space so Godot applies the stretch transform. Add a regression test using a project with `content_scale_size` != window size.

## Impact
HIGH — selector-based clicking is a core capability and silently mis-targets on any stretched project. `success:true` is returned even though nothing was hit.
close_reason: Already fixed on main (6155cd4, 2026-06-01): _node_window_position() helper in input_simulator.gd maps canvas-space via get_global_transform_with_canvas()+get_stretch_transform() into window space; regression test contentscale_click_test.go + fixture present. Worker verified empty diff/clean vet/green tests. Stale duplicate.

title: text: selector loose-matches labels; godot_click silently clicks first of multiple matches
description:
## Summary
`text:` selector matching is loose (substring + case-insensitive), and `godot_click` silently clicks the FIRST match when a selector resolves to multiple nodes — returning `success:true` even when the first match is a non-interactive node.

## Evidence (downstream-game, 2026-06-01)
- Selector `text:CONTINUE` matched TWO nodes (`godot_find_nodes` count=2):
  1. a Label whose text is "Continue from day 8, 13:00?" (descriptive copy — matched on substring "Continue")
  2. the actual Button whose text is "CONTINUE"
- `godot_click(selector:"text:CONTINUE")` clicked the FIRST match — the Label (clicked_at (960,544.5) = Label center) — which is non-interactive, so nothing happened. Returned `success:true`.

## Two sub-issues
1. **Loose matching**: `text:` matches substrings case-insensitively, so descriptive labels collide with button captions. Consider exact-match-first semantics, or a way to request exact match.
2. **Silent ambiguity on click**: when a click selector matches >1 node, prefer interactive controls (Button/etc.) and/or warn/error rather than silently clicking match[0]. At minimum, surface match count in the result.

## Proposed fix
- In `godot_click`, when the selector matches multiple nodes, rank interactive controls first (BaseButton and friends), and include `matched=N` in the result. Optionally error when ambiguous and none is clearly interactive.
- Document `text:` matching semantics; consider `text=` for exact vs `text:` for contains.

## Impact
MEDIUM — leads to false-positive `success:true` clicks that do nothing, which is hard to debug (looks like the click worked).
close_reason: Merged to main in 739d654 (commit 70ab684): selector click disambiguation, text= exact selector, matched/ambiguous in result. go vet+test pass, addon strict-mode clean.

title: godot_evaluate cannot resolve engine singletons (Engine/OS/...) and lacks ternary support
description:
## Summary
`godot_evaluate` cannot resolve engine global singletons, and does not support conditional (ternary) expressions.

## Evidence (downstream-game, 2026-06-01)
- `Engine.get_physics_frames()` -> "Execution error: Invalid named index 'Engine' for base type Object". Project autoloads (e.g. `SimManager`, `get_node(...)`, `get_viewport()`) resolve fine, but core singletons (`Engine`, and likely `OS`, `Time`, `Input`, `DisplayServer`, `ProjectSettings`) do not.
- `str(...) + str(x if cond else y)` -> "Parse error: Expected ',' or ')'". The evaluator appears not to support inline `a if cond else b` conditional expressions.
- Also: reading a script instance var via `get_node(path)._var` -> "Invalid named index '_var' for base type Object" (node returned as base Object, script members not exposed) — may be related context/whitelisting.

## Proposed fix
- Add the core engine singletons to the evaluator's identifier resolution whitelist (`Engine`, `OS`, `Time`, `Input`, `DisplayServer`, `ProjectSettings`, etc.).
- Support GDScript conditional expressions in the evaluator grammar, or document the limitation.
- Investigate exposing script-declared members on resolved nodes.

## Impact
LOW — workarounds exist (most state is reachable via autoloads / get_game_state), but the gaps are surprising and cost a few round-trips.
close_reason: Merged to main (93c6eff, commit 8cada63): engine singletons bound as Expression inputs; ternary documented as inherent Expression limitation; script-members confirmed working. GdUnit4 test added. go vet/test pass, addon strict-mode clean (verified on alt port; 26700 held by external downstream-game instance).

title: Unauthenticated Stagehand server binds all interfaces and exposes unsafe automation
description:
## Problem

`TCPServer.listen(_port)` omits `bind_address`; Godot defaults to `*`, so the addon listens on all IPv4/IPv6 interfaces. The WebSocket protocol authenticates no client. `STAGEHAND_INSTANCE_TOKEN` is only echoed by `ping` for launcher identity and does not gate requests. The exposed surface includes property mutation, method calls, input injection, scene changes, and expression evaluation with engine singletons.

## Evidence

- `addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd:56,138-169,263-276`
- `addons/stagehand/core/expression_evaluator.gd:3-16`
- Godot TCPServer docs: default bind address is `*`.

This turns a trusted development control surface into a network-reachable one wherever the host firewall permits access.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch a project with `--stagehand` and no explicit bind-address configuration.
2. Inspect the listening socket and observe it is bound to all interfaces because `TCPServer.listen()` defaults to `*`.
3. Connect a WebSocket client without `STAGEHAND_INSTANCE_TOKEN` and call `get_tree` or another automation method.
4. Observe the request succeeds without authentication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Default bind is explicit loopback only (`127.0.0.1` and/or `::1`).
- Remote bind requires an explicit opt-in setting and emits a prominent warning.
- Every automation request is rejected until the client authenticates with a per-session secret; launcher identity echo alone is not treated as authentication.
- `evaluate` and arbitrary method calls have an explicit unsafe-capability opt-in or equivalent hard boundary.
- Tests prove an unauthenticated client cannot execute any mutating or evaluation method.
- README contains a concise trust-boundary and threat-model section.

title: Persisted editor toggle can enable Stagehand in exported production builds
description:
## Problem

The editor toolbar writes `stagehand/server/enabled` through `ProjectSettings.save()`. - The toolbar toggle is session-scoped or stored in editor-only metadata, not exported ProjectSettings.

- Existing projects with the stale persisted setting are migrated or safely ignored.
- Automated tests cover editor play, debug export, and release export activation behavior.

description:

title: Accessibility tree integration (AccessKit on Godot 4.5+)
description:
## Feature

Integrate with Godot 4.5+'s AccessKit accessibility tree to provide semantic game state queries. Instead of relying only on node paths and class names, agents could query the accessibility tree for roles, labels, and relationships.

## Background

Godot 4.5 adds AccessKit support for Control nodes (screen reader support). This exposes an accessibility tree parallel to the scene tree, with semantic information like roles (button, text field, label), accessible names, and states (focused, pressed, expanded).

## Design

### New MCP Tool: `godot_get_accessibility_tree`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|

| `role:` | `"role:button"` | Nodes with AccessKit role "button" |

- Use AccessKit bridge APIs to enumerate accessible nodes
- Fall back gracefully on Godot < 4.5 with clear error message

title: quit-on-disconnect fires against a never-connected instance, killing hand-rolled launches
description:
The anti-zombie self-quit (`QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS = 10000`, `stagehand_server.gd:22`) also fires against an instance that has **never** had a client, if the operator does not connect within the grace window. For a hand-rolled launch — currently required for the Windows GUI binary on WSL — the game silently disappears mid-setup.

Observed 2026-07-25, addon 0.3.1, downstream-game. Launched headless, spent ~30s reading the port/token out of the log and loading the MCP tool schemas, then connected:

    Stagehand: Server listening on port 26700 (127.0.0.1)
    Stagehand: No client reconnected within 10000ms of the last disconnect
               — quitting (opt out with STAGEHAND_QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT=0)
    Stagehand: Server stopped

    godot_connect -> dial 127.0.0.1:26700: connect: connection refused

The message says "reconnected ... since the last disconnect", but there had been no client and no disconnect, so the log reads as a non-sequitur and the real trigger (a manual launch is on a human/agent clock, not a launcher's) is not obvious. `_had_client` at `stagehand_server.gd:212` is meant to guard exactly this — worth confirming whether it is actually gating the timer in the never-connected case, since the observed behaviour is a quit without any client ever attaching.

Not a correctness bug — `STAGEHAND_QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT=0` opts out and the zombie guard is worth keeping. Ergonomics only. Options: a longer initial grace before the first client attaches than between reconnects; or a distinct startup message naming `STAGEHAND_QUIT_ON_DISCONNECT=0` up front when the server starts and no launcher handshake is expected.

title: Add README status badges (issues, PRs, license, coverage)
description:
Match the badge row used in mrf/newrelic_exporter. README.md now carries no
badges at all: the Go Report Card badge was removed because goreportcard.com is
deprecated (owner call, 2026-07-25).

## Producer split (decided 2026-07-25)

**go-ci-report-card is the sole producer of Go metrics.** This ticket does not
compute Go coverage, gofmt rates, vet results or anything else about the Go
code. It renders what the report card already produced. Blocked on
godot-stagehand-go-ci-report-card-r0ri for that reason.

What this ticket owns:
- the issues / PRs / license badges (pure shields.io lookups, no CI work)
- reading the Go coverage number the report card emits and turning it into a
  badge
- the Godot/GDScript metric, which the report card cannot see at all

## Badges to add

```markdown
[![GitHub issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/mrf/godot-stagehand)](https://github.com/mrf/godot-stagehand/issues)
[![GitHub pull requests](https://img.shields.io/github/issues-pr/mrf/godot-stagehand)](https://github.com/mrf/godot-stagehand/pulls)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/mrf/godot-stagehand)](LICENSE)
[![Go coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrf/godot-stagehand/badges/coverage-go-badge.svg)](https://mrf.github.io/godot-stagehand/)
[![Godot coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrf/godot-stagehand/badges/coverage-godot-badge.svg)](https://github.com/mrf/godot-stagehand/actions)
```

The Go coverage badge links to the report card page, since that is where the
number comes from and where a reader can see the rest of the Go scoring.

Do NOT re-add a goreportcard.com badge.

## Two coverage numbers, never one blended figure

This project is two codebases behind one name: the Go server/CLI and the
GDScript addon. Averaging them, or quoting only the one that is easy to measure,
produces a number that is technically true and practically a lie. Publish them
separately and label each for exactly what it measures.

**Badge 1: Go coverage.** Consume it from the report card, do not recompute.
r0ri is responsible for emitting the figure in a machine-readable form and for
making sure it was measured with a real Godot binary and the `godot` build tag
enabled. If that value is not yet exposed, extend the report card rather than
adding a second coverage run here.

**Badge 2: Godot/GDScript coverage.** Cover addons/stagehand/ from the GdUnit4
suite. This is genuinely this ticket work: the report card scores Go only and
has no view of the addon.

Do NOT assume this is a solved problem. Before building it, verify whether
GdUnit4 in the pinned Godot version can emit line coverage at all. If it cannot,
do not synthesise a percentage and do not quietly reuse the Go number. Either:
- report an honestly-labelled proxy the badge names precisely, for example
  "addon files under test: N/M" rather than the word "coverage"; or
- omit the second badge and say in the README why the addon is not
  line-covered.

A missing badge is honest. A badge labelled "coverage" that is measuring
something else is not, and this project sells itself to people who care about
test rigour.

## Mechanism

Port the badge-publishing steps from mrf/newrelic_exporter
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml (lines 65-104):

1. Take the percentage (from the report card for Go, from the GdUnit4 step for
   the addon).
2. Pick a colour by threshold (>=80 brightgreen, >=60 yellow, >=40 orange, else
   red) and fetch the SVG from `img.shields.io/badge/<label>-<pct>%25-<colour>`.
3. Commit both SVGs to an orphan `badges` branch and force-push. The README
   reads them from raw.githubusercontent.com.

Three things must change when porting, or it silently no-ops:

- The reference workflow gates on `refs/heads/master`. This repo default branch
  is `main`.
- The job needs `permissions: contents: write` to push the badges branch.
- Keep `continue-on-error: true` on the push step so a badge failure never reds
  a real CI run.

## Done when

- Five badges render on the repo front page.
- The Go coverage badge shows the same number as the report card page. If they
  can disagree, the badge is being computed in the wrong place.
- The Godot badge measures what its label claims, or is absent with a README
  sentence explaining why.
- A comment beside the GDScript CI step records what that number covers and
  what it excludes.

title: set_property: boolean values arrive as String, breaking the write AND crashing the jzs read-back fix
description:
godot-stagehand-jzs (commit c84ef41, "success now reflects a post-set read-back") does not fix the falsy-value round-trip bug it targeted, and introduces a worse regression: godot_set_property now returns an empty {} response for ANY boolean value on ANY property.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via temporary instrumentation in a downstream consumer, downstream-project, 2026-07-14 — reproduced on a genuinely fresh Godot process, verified via taskkill.exe + new PID each run):

Boolean values sent through the godot_set_property MCP tool's `value` parameter arrive in the GDScript handler (property_handler.gd set_property()) as native GDScript String ("true"/"false"), NOT as bool. Confirmed via direct instrumentation:
  params.get("value") -> typeof() == TYPE_STRING (4), type_string() == "String"
for both value:true and value:false requests.

CONSEQUENCE A (the original jzs bug, still present): Object.set(property, "true"/"false") on a strictly bool-typed GDScript script member (e.g. `var running: bool = true`, no custom setter) silently no-ops -- the String value is rejected by the typed assignment without error, and the property is left unchanged. This is exactly the original godot-stagehand-jzs symptom (success:true reported, write never applied) and it is NOT fixed.

CONSEQUENCE B (new regression introduced by c84ef41): the fix's new line
  return { "success": applied_value == requested_value, ... }
compares applied_value (bool, unchanged) against requested_value (String) via `==` inside compiled (non-Expression) GDScript. This throws an uncaught runtime error ("Invalid operands 'bool' and 'String' in operator '=='" class of error) that aborts set_property() mid-execution. The aborted call returns null instead of a Dictionary, which _dispatch_and_respond's await handler.call(params) propagates, and the client receives an EMPTY {} JSON-RPC result -- no success, no error, no previous_value. This reproduced identically for a GDScript script property (SimManager.running) and a native engine property (Camera3D.current), so it is not specific to script-level properties.

WHERE TO LOOK: the value almost certainly arrives as a string well before property_handler.gd -- likely in the Go server's JSON encoding of the `value` MCP tool argument (tools_property.go's handleSetProperty forwards `args["value"]` verbatim to callGodotInstance), or in the addon's WebSocket JSON-RPC decode path (protocol/json_rpc.gd) that turns the wire message into the `params` Dictionary GDScript receives. get_property/evaluate paths are unaffected (they don't send a `value` argument), so this is specific to how `value` round-trips through the MCP tool schema (mcp.WithAny("value", ...)) and/or Go->JSON->GDScript serialization.

REGRESSION TESTS THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS: c84ef41 added TestSmokeSetPropertyFalsyValues (round-trips false/0/""/null) and TestSmokeSetPropertyReportsFailureOnRejectedSet, both in internal/godotconn/godot_integration_test.go. Neither caught this because they must be exercising the property_handler.gd path directly (or via a mechanism that preserves native types) rather than the full MCP-tool-call -> Go server -> WebSocket -> GDScript round trip a real client uses. Recommend adding an end-to-end regression test that goes through the actual mcp.CallToolRequest path (like tools_property.go's own handleSetProperty) with a real bool argument, asserting the GDScript-side received type is TYPE_BOOL, not TYPE_STRING.

IMPACT: godot_set_property is currently unusable for boolean values against any consumer project. Consumers must use godot_evaluate's set() as a workaround (documented in downstream-project's docs/media/README.md). See downstream-project ks-stagehand-set-property-falsy-noop-1hs for the full downstream investigation and evidence trail.

title: set_property: value arrives as JSON String — all int/float/Vector sets now hard-fail (regression from v0.3.0 bool workaround)
description:
set_property's `value` argument reaches GDScript as a JSON **String**, not a native Variant. In v0.3.0 this is masked for bool (the addon string-parses "true"/"false") but breaks every numeric and composite target — including cases that WORKED before v0.3.0.

CONFIRMED MECHANISM (live, godot-stagehand 0.3.0, Godot 4.6.2 headless Linux, downstream consumer downstream-game, 2026-07-25):

Probe — set a String-typed property to a JSON object, then read it back:
  set_property /root/SimManager editor_description = {"x": 11.7, "y": 7.55, "z": 19.7}
    -> {"previous_value":"","success":true}
  evaluate [type_string(typeof(...editor_description)), ...editor_description]
    -> ["String", "{\"x\": 11.7, \"y\": 7.55, \"z\": 19.7}"]

The stored value is the RAW JSON TEXT I sent — note `{"x"` with no space after the brace. Godot's own str(Dictionary) renders `{ "x": 11.7, ... }` WITH a space, so this is provably the wire bytes, not a stringified Dictionary.

CONTRAST — call_method's `args` marshal correctly:
  call_method /root/SimManager set_meta ["probe", {"x":11.7,"y":7.55,"z":19.7}]
  evaluate [type_string(typeof(get_meta("probe"))), str(get_meta("probe"))]
    -> ["Dictionary", "{ \"x\": 11.7, \"y\": 7.55, \"z\": 19.7 }"]   <-- native Dictionary, Godot spacing

So the JSON-RPC decode path is fine in general; the defect is specific to how set_property's `value` is encoded (tools_property.go handleSetProperty / mcp.WithAny("value")), exactly where godot-stagehand-set-property-bool-string-coercion-5fz predicted.

WHY BOOL LOOKS FIXED: property_handler.gd `_coerce_json_value` has an explicit TYPE_BOOL case that parses the String "true"/"false". That is a targeted workaround for the symptom, not a fix for the stringification. String-typed targets also pass (the String falls through and assigns cleanly). Every other target type has no string-parsing path — `_coerce_int`/`_coerce_float` accept only native int/float, and `_json_component` requires a real Dictionary/Array — so they now hard-fail the conversion gate.

LIVE RESULTS (v0.3.0):
  PASS  bool  running=false -> success, read-back false (native bool), sim ticks froze (379, 379)
  PASS  bool  running=true  -> success, read-back true, ticks resumed 379 -> 456
  PASS  String editor_description="" -> success
  FAIL  int   elapsed_ticks=0  -> invalid_value "Invalid value for property" (target_type=int)
  FAIL  int   elapsed_ticks=5  -> invalid_value  (so it is NOT falsy-specific — ALL ints fail)
  FAIL  float fov=50           -> invalid_value (target_type=float)
  FAIL  Vector3 position={"x":11.7,"y":7.55,"z":19.7} -> "Value cannot be converted to Vector3"
  FAIL  Vector3 position=[11.7,7.55,19.7]             -> same

REGRESSION, not a pre-existing gap: downstream-game ticket (set_property falsy-noop) records (2026-07-17, pre-re-vendor) "scalar float writes on the SAME node work fine (set_property fov=50 round-tripped correctly)". Same node, same property, same value now errors. Inference (NOT instrumented): before the coercion gate existed the raw String was handed straight to Object.set(), and Godot's permissive Variant conversion turned "50" into 50.0; the new strict gate rejects it first. The stringification itself may well predate v0.3.0 — what changed is that it is now fatal instead of silently absorbed.

Silver lining: nothing lies anymore. Failed sets return a loud invalid_value error and leave the property untouched (verified: fov still 75.0 after the failed write). The original "success:true but never applied" silent-lie class is gone.

FIX DIRECTION: stop stringifying `value` on the Go side so it arrives as a native JSON type; then the addon's existing coercion handles the rest and the TYPE_BOOL string-parsing special case can stay as belt-and-braces. Regression coverage must go through the real MCP-tool -> Go -> WebSocket -> GDScript round trip (5fz already flagged that the existing tests bypass it) and assert the GDScript-side received TYPE for bool, int, float, String, Vector2, Vector3, Vector2i, Color — not just the round-tripped value.
