title: CLI validates selectors only after connecting
description:
One-shot CLI commands dial Godot before validating their selector/params, so a malformed selector reports a connection failure (exit 3) instead of a usage error (exit 2); a user with no game running never learns the selector was bad.

Repro (build SHA 94a9995, no game running):
  STAGEHAND_AUTH_TOKEN=x ./godot-stagehand find "" --port 26799 --timeout 2s
  actual:   error: connect to Godot at 127.0.0.1:26799: dial tcp ...: connection refused   (rc=3)
  expected: error: selector is empty  (rc=2, per the exit-code table in --help: 2=usage, 3=connection)

An empty selector is definitively invalid -- internal/selector/parse.go:64 returns `selector is empty`. Validation lives inside `gwpop.Execute` (internal/gwpop/gwpop.go:327 runs selector.ParseChain over Spec.Selectors params), which internal/cli/commands.go only reaches after the session is established (e.g. commands.go:36, :531). CLAUDE.md convention 5 says selectors are validated in Go before being sent to Godot; that holds literally, but the check should run before the dial so bad input is a usage error regardless of whether a game is up.

title: StagehandServer should default to PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS so paused-tree games can connect
description:
## Summary

`StagehandServer` polls its TCP/WebSocket loop in `_process()`, but the autoload does **not** set `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. In any host game that pauses the SceneTree (e.g. at startup for an intro/menu overlay), `_process()` never fires while paused, so the server **accepts the TCP connection but never completes the WebSocket handshake**. The client sees the TCP socket establish and then times out on the handshake read.

Make the server default to `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` so it keeps servicing its socket loop regardless of tree pause state. It's a pure-networking node with no gameplay side effects, so always-processing is safe and correct.

## Symptom (as seen by the client)

`godot_connect` / `godot_launch` fail with, e.g.:

```
dial 127.0.0.1:26700: read tcp 127.0.0.1:45654->127.0.0.1:26700: i/o timeout
```

The TCP three-way handshake completes (source port assigned, connection ESTABLISHED) — it is the WebSocket upgrade that hangs. Reproduced live 2026-07-25 against the vendored 0.3.1 addon in a headless Linux Godot run of a game that pauses the tree at boot; the server log shows `Server listening on port 26700` with zero errors, yet no connection can complete.

## Root cause

`addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd` runs its accept/poll in `_process()`. With the default `PROCESS_MODE_INHERIT`, a paused SceneTree freezes that loop. There is currently no `process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` anywhere in the file (confirmed: `grep -c PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` = 0 at tag v0.3.1).

This is the same class of freeze already documented downstream as a tree-pause deadlock (pausing via `godot_evaluate` freezes the server so the un-pause command never processes).

## Proposed fix

In `StagehandServer._ready()` (or as a node property), set:

```gdscript
process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
```

so the socket loop runs even when `get_tree().paused == true`.

## Test guard (please add)

A regression test that **launches with the tree paused, then asserts a client can connect and complete the handshake**. Without this guard the property is trivially dropped by a refactor and the regression is silent — see history below.

## Downstream history (why this matters / keeps recurring)

A downstream game carries this exact fix as a local patch and has now lost it **twice** to wholesale addon re-vendors:

- `da04b75c` (2026-05-18) added `process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` — commit msg: *"Game.gd pauses the scene tree at startup for the opening dispatch. Without PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, _process() never fires ... so TCP connections are accepted but WebSocket handshake never completes."*
- Dropped at the downstream-game re-pin `5d1410ec` (2026-06-10) when the addon was re-vendored from upstream.
- Still absent through the 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 pin bumps.

Landing this upstream (as the default) means downstream re-pins stop silently reintroducing the bug. Fixing it upstream is the whole reason to file here rather than re-patch locally again.
close_reason: Merged 1680bd2: StagehandServer PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS + paused-tree regression test

title: Port flag --stagehand-port= is silently ignored unless passed after a -- separator
description:
`--stagehand-port=N` is documented as working in any argument position, but `_get_port()` (`addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd:844`) scans only `OS.get_cmdline_user_args()`, which Godot populates exclusively with arguments appearing **after** a `--` separator. A flag placed before `--` is silently ignored and the server falls back to `DEFAULT_PORT` (26700).

    static func _get_port() -> int:
        var env_port: String = OS.get_environment("STAGEHAND_PORT")
        if env_port != "" and env_port.is_valid_int():
            return env_port.to_int()
        for arg: String in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():      # <-- post-`--` args only
            if arg.begins_with("--stagehand-port="):
                ...
        return DEFAULT_PORT

Observed 2026-07-25, addon 0.3.1, downstream-game:

    STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 STAGEHAND_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1 ~/.local/bin/godot-4.6.2-linux \
      --path . --headless --stagehand --stagehand-port=26711
    -> Stagehand: Server listening on port 26700 (127.0.0.1)

Silent, so it presents as a mystery port collision rather than a rejected flag.

`godot_launch` is unaffected — it already passes `-- --stagehand`, i.e. after the separator (`pgrep`: `godot-4.6.2-linux --headless --path /home/user/Projects/downstream-game -- --stagehand`). This only bites hand-rolled launches, which the WSL GUI path currently requires (see the `godot_launch` WSL ticket).

Options: also scan `OS.get_cmdline_args()`, or correct the docs/skill guidance to state the flag must follow `--` and point at `STAGEHAND_PORT` as the position-independent route. At minimum, warn when `--stagehand-port=` is seen in `get_cmdline_args()` but not `get_cmdline_user_args()`.

title: Add CLI and scenario runner for CI and human debugging
description:
## Problem

Stagehand is MCP-only. That is effective for agents but leaves CI pipelines, deterministic test harnesses, and human debugging without an executable interface. The current README claims direct CI/test-runner use while `docs/architecture/mcp-vs-cli.md` explicitly says those workflows require an MCP client.

## Scope

Add a protocol-agnostic CLI frontend and a scenario runner on top of `godotconn`, `selector`, and `launch`. Preserve current no-argument stdio MCP behavior for compatibility. Support one-shot inspection/actions plus a declarative sequence of launch/connect, action, wait, assertion, screenshot/diff, and cleanup steps. Produce machine-readable results and test artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Existing no-argument invocation remains an MCP stdio server.
- One-shot commands cover connect/status/tree/find/property/call/input/wait/screenshot/performance.
- `godot-stagehand run <scenario>` executes ordered actions, waits, and assertions without an MCP client.
- Failures return stable nonzero exit codes and actionable diagnostics.
- Scenario runs can emit JSON, JUnit XML, screenshots/diffs, Godot logs, and an RPC timing trace.
- CI contains a real-Godot scenario-runner smoke gate.
- README CI claims use this executable workflow.

title: Addon installation breaks host project compilation (GDScript parse errors)
description:
## Problem

- `core/selector_engine.gd:322` — uses `parent.tree` but Node has no `.tree` property. Must be `parent.get_tree()`.

**Showstopper.** Any Godot project that installs this addon cannot compile. Manual testing proved this — the addon blocked downstream-game from building.

- [ ] All GDScript files parse without errors in Godot 4.2+ (test with `--check-only` or `--headless --quit`)
- [ ] Addon installed into a clean Godot project does NOT break compilation
- [ ] Add a CI/smoke check that validates addon GDScript parses cleanly

## TDD Protocol

Write a test (Go integration test that launches Godot with the addon and asserts clean startup) BEFORE fixing the GDScript. The test must fail first, then pass after the fix.

title: wait_for_property: stringified expected_value never matches, wait sits out its full timeout
description:
Follow-up from godot-stagehand-set-property-value-stringified-e7er (merged a7da1c5). Filed from that worker's .orchestrator-note, section 'Scope call I made'.

## What the e7er worker DID fix

godot_wait_for_property's expected_value had the identical untyped-schema defect as set_property's value — a bare mcp.WithAny emits no 'type' key, leaving clients nothing to marshal against. The worker applied the same one-line Go schema fix (withJSONTypeUnion) at internal/mcpserver/tools_wait.go:154 and extended the schema test to cover it, on the grounds that leaving the identical root cause unfixed would be a half-fix. That part is DONE and merged.

## What it deliberately did NOT fix — this ticket

The GDScript-side defensive string-parsing was extended into property_handler.gd but NOT into waiter.gd. The worker's stated reason: it is a larger behavior change with distinct semantics per operator (equals on a String property, contains, gt/lt) and needs its own tests. That is a sound scope call, not an oversight.

## The residual gap (worker's words: 'unverified against a live client but visible in the code')

- waiter.gd:40 compares actual_value == expected_value. A stringified \"5\" never equals an int 5, so the wait silently sits out its FULL timeout rather than failing fast.
- waiter.gd:60-66 gt/lt guard on 'expected_value is float or int', so a stringified numeric likewise never matches.

Symptom for a user: wait_for_property appears to hang, then times out, against a property that actually holds the expected value. The Go schema fix makes this much less likely (a conforming client now sends native types), but v0.3.0 shipped to clients we do not control, which is exactly why set_property got belt-and-braces GDScript parsing too.

## NOT YET REPRODUCED

This is inferred from reading waiter.gd, not observed. Per the repo debugging rules: reproduce it with a failing test FIRST — mirror TestMCPSetPropertyAcceptsStringifiedClientValues (internal/mcpserver/set_property_godot_test.go, added by e7er) which enters through MCPServer.HandleMessage and crosses the real WebSocket to the real GDScript handler. If it does NOT reproduce, close this with that evidence rather than fixing speculatively.

## Design constraint inherited from e7er

Target-awareness is load-bearing. property_handler.gd's _parse_stringified_json only JSON-decodes when the target type cannot hold text, so text_prop = \"50\" still stores two characters. Any waiter.gd equivalent must preserve that: 'equals' against a String property must still compare text literally. Also use JSON.new().parse(), not JSON.parse_string() — the latter pushes an engine error into the host game's log on every non-JSON string.

Also worth knowing (probed live on Godot 4.6.2 during e7er): JSON.parse_string(\"50\") returns float 50.0, not int.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `godot_wait_for_signal` (or similar wait tool) on a signal that hasn't fired yet
2. Close the game window / kill the Godot process / trigger game-over
3. Observe the MCP tool call never returns

## Expected Behavior

Wait tools should detect WebSocket disconnection and return an error (e.g., `"error": "connection lost while waiting for signal X"`) within a reasonable timeout.

## Actual Behavior

The MCP server hangs forever waiting for a response that will never arrive.

## Impact

Any automation or test script using wait tools becomes permanently stuck if the game exits unexpectedly. Requires manual kill of the MCP process.

## Suggested Fix

- Detect WebSocket close/error in the wait loop and abort with a descriptive error
- Optionally add a configurable timeout parameter to all wait tools (default e.g. 30s)

title: setup skips stale installed addon without version warning
description:

title: wait/input misreport misplaced --port flag
description:
Build 5c22cb0. `godot-stagehand wait --port 26788 node name:Ghost --timeout 3s` fails with:

    error: --port is required: the addon's default 26700 is shared and may belong to another agent's game; pass the port your instance printed at startup

The user DID pass --port; the real problem is that `wait` and `input` take a positional subcommand first, so `--port` is consumed as the subcommand name (internal/cli/commands.go:357 `sub, rest := args[0], args[1:]`, same pattern at the `input` dispatch ~line 342). The session port check (internal/cli/session.go:92) fires before the `default:` unknown-subcommand branch (commands.go:342, :416), so the accurate error is never reached.

`property` handles the identical case correctly: `property --port 26799` -> `error: unknown property subcommand "--port" (want get or set)` (commands.go:132). Expected: wait/input give the same accurate message. Actual: they claim a flag the user supplied is missing, sending users to debug the wrong thing. Repro is deterministic and needs no running Godot.

title: setup rejects --force after project path
description:

title: Default diff dir is CWD-relative, baselines scenario-relative
description:
Build d244780. internal/scenario/runner.go:427-444 resolveDirs(): the default baseline dir goes through r.sc.resolve("stagehand-baselines"), which session.go:159-166 documents as making the path absolute against the scenario file's own directory 'so a scenario file can be run from any working directory'. The default diff dir does not: runner.go:441-443 sets r.diffDir = "stagehand-diffs" as a bare relative string with no resolve().

Repro: run any scenario containing a failing screenshot_diff without --out-dir, from a directory other than the one holding the scenario file. Expected: diff artifacts land next to the baselines (scenario-relative stagehand-diffs/), consistent with the documented resolve() contract. Actual: <name>-actual.png and <name>-diff.png are written into the current working directory's stagehand-diffs/, so the same scenario scatters artifacts to a different place on every invocation and the paths recorded in report.json / junit.xml are not reproducible.

Secondary: the mismatch also means a run with no --out-dir writes files into the user's CWD without warning, while the plain `screenshot` action deliberately writes nothing at all in that case (runner.go:300-302) — the two artifact paths behave inconsistently. docs/cli.md:146 documents baseline_dir as scenario-relative and says nothing about where diffs go.

title: godot_evaluate context_node param silently ignored
description: The Go MCP server (tools_method.go:138) sends the context_node parameter as key "context_node" in the JSON-RPC params dict, but the Godot expression_evaluator.gd (line 24) reads the key "selector" instead. title: godot_press_key cannot target a specific embedded subwindow
description:
input_key still goes through Input.parse_input_event, which the engine routes to whichever window holds focus. Verified against Godot 4.6.2 (87s.21 probes): a freshly-popped AcceptDialog has focus and receives a synthesized Escape, but there is no way to address a key at a named window. A godot_press_key 'window' parameter, or an explicit focus-restoring action, would let a caller recover instead of being stuck. Deliberately out of scope for 87s.21: grabbing focus mutates app state the caller did not request.
